title: Your Graph Recommenders are Provably Doing Graph Contrastive Learning

problem.claim: Graph recommenders extract information from user-item interaction graphs, while graph contrastive learning trains graph neural networks with contrastive objectives and is often used jointly with supervised recommendation loss.

gap.claim: The theoretical relationship between graph recommenders and graph contrastive learning is poorly understood.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph recommenders are graph neural network encoders specialized for user-item interaction graphs and have attracted attention because of strong recommendation performance.
Graph contrastive learning is a popular direction for learning graph neural networks with contrastive objectives and is widely combined with supervised recommendation loss.
Despite overlap between the two areas, their theoretical relationship remains sparsely understood, which the authors associate with inefficient research.

unknowns: The abstract units do not state the paper's method, theorem, or formal result.
No experiments, datasets, baselines, quantitative findings, or limitations are supplied.
